title: Dust Pricing: Pro and Max Plan Costs for 2026
summary: Dust pricing offers Pro ($24–30/seat/month) and Max ($120–150) tiers. Calculate costs across your team size to determine which plan fits your budget.
body_markdown:
## Automating around Dust with Activepieces


Only if Dust's answers have to land somewhere else does Activepieces matter. Even then it adds a second tool to run and pay for, because it doesn't replace Dust or shrink its bill.


What it does bill is the run: its published pricing lists 1 credit per flow run however many steps the flow has, and the Free plan carries 1,000 credits a month across unlimited flows, where Zapier bills per task and Make per module.


Staying inside a single vendor's models is cheap until you need the output elsewhere; that's where this work starts.


### When Dust needs a separate workflow tool


Your support lead asks an agent to summarize a customer thread, and then someone copies that summary into the CRM by hand. Then again for the next thread, and the one after.


Dust agents are good at the answering. Moving the answer into other software is separate work, and it's the work that quietly eats hours.


If a Dust result has to trigger something, such as a ticket, a new row, or an update to a customer record, you need something that carries it across. Doing that by hand is a cost your seat price never shows.


### Sending Dust outputs to your existing tools


Activepieces carries a Dust agent's output into the CRM, ticketing system or spreadsheet your team already uses, through 750 integrations, roughly 60% of them community-contributed, on an MIT-licensed core, so your existing tooling will likely integrate without custom work.


The Dust agent produces the output, and an Activepieces flow receives it and branches it onward.


The same diagram shows a plain Dust chat path running alongside, with no flow attached. Read the two paths side by side: chat ends at a person reading an answer, while the flow ends with records changed in other tools.


The next question is cost. The flow adds its own setup, upkeep, and plan, so count it as a line item beside your Dust usage, not a discount on it.


Skip Activepieces if your team only chats with documents and reads the answers. The same goes if the handoff happens a few times a month, where copying is cheaper than maintaining a flow.


Build one when a person is repeating the same copy-and-paste every day, and not before.
